alex (Support): Hi — escalating a customer issue. Org Greenleaf seeing recurring 429s for model redwood-7b-instruct. Symptoms: bursts of short requests mixed with large-context prompts (~5.5k tokens) during a migration job. They report '429 Rate limit exceeded' and a Retry-After around 10-15s. Headers they copied: `x-rate-limit-model: 600rpm/36000tpm`, `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d`. Can SRE confirm whether this looks like per-model RPM/TPM exhaustion vs concurrency throttling?

maria (SRE): Thanks — can you paste a minimal repro (curl) + timestamps the customer saw the 429s? Also send the org id so we can correlate in rate-limiter logs. From the symptoms it could be a TPM burst: long contexts consume many tokens and make you hit token-minute limits faster than RPM.

alex (Support): Pasting the curl the customer used (sanitized):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-instruct","input":"<~5500-token prompt>","max_tokens":512}'
```

They also ran a short-burst loop (20 reqs in ~15s) right before the failures. Their timestamps: first 429 at 2025-11-22T18:04:12Z, last at 2025-11-22T18:11:03Z.

maria (SRE): I ran a quick repro locally: spun 30 concurrent workers sending ~3500-token prompts to `redwood-7b-instruct` for 2 minutes. Observed the rate-limiter tripping and returning 429 + `Retry-After` header. Notes from the run:
- Shared-tier per-model soft limits we enforce: ~600 RPM (requests per minute) and ~36000 TPM (tokens per minute) for this model.
- Max practical concurrency for this model on shared pools is ~8 concurrent active generation streams; above that we start queuing and may return 429s for fairness/backpressure.
- Long contexts accelerate TPM usage: a 5k-token context + 512 tokens generated counts ~5512 tokens against TPM.

So in short: their mix of bursts + long contexts is hitting the token-minute cap rather than a pure request-RPM cap.

ken (Product): For customers with this access pattern we recommend a few options: 1) client-side pacing (limit concurrent requests and add exponential backoff with jitter), 2) migrate to Dedicated for reserved capacity and higher per-model limits, or 3) request a temporary quota bump from support while they refactor. I'll prepare a short doc to outline tradeoffs.

alex (Support): Shared this repro advice with the customer and asked them to run a few defensive steps. Requested: full cURL -v output (including response headers), the `x-request-id` values, and timestamps for a 10-minute window. I also gave them a short mitigation snippet to reduce immediate 429s:
```python
# basic client-side pacing example
import time, requests
from random import uniform

SEMAPHORE = 6  # cap concurrency to 6 for this model on shared tier
for i in range(100):
    # perform work then sleep to avoid bursts
    requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload)
    time.sleep(uniform(0.15, 0.5))  # jittered pacing
```

maria (SRE): Additional repro/fixes we need from customer: full request payload sizes (tokenized length if available), their traffic pattern (QPS over sliding windows), and the exact model name + region. With that we can correlate `org_id` in the rate-limiter logs and produce a timeline. If we confirm TPM exhaustion we can offer a temporary token-rate increase or recommend short-term batching changes (e.g., move heavy contexts to async/gated pipelines).

alex (Support): Customer sent the logs (org_id: org_903f). I started a ticket for a temporary bump but flagged SRE to verify.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2468 created (rate-limit spike for org_903f). Paging @maria.

maria (SRE): I'll pull the rate-limiter traces now. Quick note on diagnostics: when checking logs look for these keys -> `model`, `org_id`, `window_type` (rpm/tpm), `window_limit`, `window_used`. That lets you tell whether an RPM window or TPM window fired. Also check for `concurrency_drop` samples which indicate we hit concurrent-stream headroom.

ken (Product): Also adding a customer-facing explanation we can send: short bullets that explain difference between RPM (requests) and TPM (tokens), why long contexts hit TPM faster, and recommended mitigations (cap concurrency, use shorter contexts, move heavy jobs to Dedicated). I'll post that doc once drafted.

alex (Support): Customer accepted immediate mitigations and will implement client-side pacing + token batching. I offered a temporary quota bump while they test. Will update thread when SRE confirms logs. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
